steps.message: If we accept a new order for 800 Hoodies on 1 April 2026, can we deliver it by 25 April 2026?

reply.answer:
Yes — 800 tops (hoodies) can be done by 25 April; the fastest all-outsourced plan finishes 6 April, well inside the deadline.

| Plan | Allocation | Estimated completion | External charge |
|---|---|---|---|
| Fastest | W8 FreshStart 300, W6 Nimble Needle 390, W2 SteadyHands 110 | 6 Apr 2026 | 911 |
| Cheapest by 25 Apr | W3 BudgetWorks 800 | 13 Apr 2026 | 640 |

The cheapest option is low risk for the date: under the full-redo assumption all 800 pieces still arrive by 25 April. W3 does carry a 9% batch defect rate and a 5-day queue, while the fastest plan has a medium overall risk with an 88% chance all batches come back clean.

Assumptions: new batch of 800 original pieces, start 1 April 2026, capacity and queues from the 2026-04-01 data; in-house production left out (no in-house cost in the data); charges exclude transport and rework; currency unspecified.

steps.message: For the same 800 Hoodies, would delivery by 3 April 2026 be feasible instead?

reply.answer:
No — 3 April 2026 is not feasible for 800 pieces through outside workshops. The most they could deliver by then is 230 pieces, leaving 570 unallocated.

Even the fastest plan, which allows in-house work plus the parallel workshops, would not be complete by 3 April: its earliest pieces arrive 5–6 April. I can't forecast in-house timing alone from the data, but the outside-workshop ceiling is the binding limit here.

Assumptions: new 800-piece batch starting 1 April, capacity and queues from the 2026-04-01 data; in-house production excluded from this cheapest check because no in-house cost per piece is recorded.

result.message: Insufficient modeled capacity within the requested horizon. Outside workshops only were compared; the fastest plan, which can add in-house capacity, gives the earliest possible date.

At most 300 pieces could go to W8; the remaining 500 would need another workshop or a second allocation.

steps.message: If the order increases from 800 to 1,600 pieces, is the original delivery date still feasible?

reply.answer:
Yes — the original 25 April 2026 date still holds at 1,600 pieces. The cheapest plan by that deadline (W3 BudgetWorks, all 1,600) completes 17 April for about 1,280.

There is a quality-exposure caveat at this size: W3 has a 9% batch rework chance, and in the full-redo scenario its arrival moves to 28 April — after the deadline. That gives roughly a 91% chance all pieces are on time. The fastest plan avoids that by splitting across W8 (300), W5 (400), W6 (650) and W2 (250) for 8 April at about 1,845, though four batches means a 17% chance at least one needs rework.

Assumptions: new 1,600-piece tops batch starting 1 April 2026, capacity and queues from the 2026-04-01 data; in-house left out of the cheapest comparison; charges exclude transport and rework; currency unspecified.
